evidence.r1: The 'Playing Next' queue, a six-row content list, floats top-right as a glass-rimmed platter (light and dark).
evidence.r2: No glass is stacked: the playlist menu opens clear of the queue platter, and the scrubber and volume tracks are fills.
evidence.r3: Four floating elements (queue, Save Queue, transport, volume), each serving the brief.
evidence.r4: Transport, volume, Save Queue and the menu share one frosted regular material.
evidence.r6: No control is tinted; play is monochrome.
evidence.r7: The queue platter's body is a flat opaque fill: pixel-uniform over the ice, and identical with reduce transparency on (light near-white, dark navy).
evidence.r8: Capsule transport, volume and Save Queue; a fixed-radius queue platter and menu.
evidence.r9: The 'Late Desk' ring and the transport contents follow their containers; no corner reads pinched.
evidence.r11: Prev/play/next and the scrubber share the transport; volume is separate; two groups in the bottom bar.
evidence.r12: The transport's buttons are all icons (the times are readouts); Save Queue is one labelled button; the menu holds only text.
evidence.r13: Material sits on the transport, volume and Save Queue themselves.
evidence.r14: Save Queue sits a deliberate gap below the queue; transport and volume are spaced apart on purpose.
evidence.r15: The page does not scroll and nothing passes under a floating control, so the rule holds vacuously.
evidence.r16: Every glass surface sits over the textured ice artwork.
evidence.r17: The title, track list and credits sit in the left column, clear of the glass; the artwork is the backdrop.
evidence.r18: Queue and transport text is at least ~4.8:1 in both schemes (the dark time readout is the lowest).
evidence.r19: Reduced capture: the 'Save Queue' label drops to the bottom edge of its capsule and is clipped.
evidence.r20: The artwork fills the window edge to edge, with the transport and volume floating over it.
evidence.r21: The left column fades the artwork with a soft wash, not a hard edge, and the track list clears the transport.
evidence.r22: The queue platter carries a custom opaque background with a drawn border instead of the material (the dark scheme's navy slab).
evidence.r23: The playlist menu opens in place of the Save Queue control, and a pointer glow shows in the dark menu.
evidence.r24: Controls are monochrome; the orange now-playing bars live in the track list.
evidence.r25: Dark labels on pale glass (light) and light labels on dark glass (dark) stand apart from the grey-blue ice.
